'North-facing' means aspect_deg within 45 deg of 0 (or aspect_class N / NE / NW)); curvature_plan (Curvature of the contour line across the slope (spurs / ridges diverge = positive, gullies / hollows converge = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. Counts layers, not independent minerals: mixed prototypes appear in more than one layer, and pyroxene/smectite variants count separately); outcrop_exposure (Height proxy for an exposed vertical section: local_relief_50m where at least 2% of the cells within 50 m have slope_2m >= 25 degrees (a steep face is actually present in the window), else 0. Unit is metres; includes the slope contribution (a smooth 30 deg ramp has a high TRI)); unit_diversity_100m (Number of distinct mapped geologic units having at least one cell within 100 m of the cell (integer stored as float). 1 = deep inside one unit, 2+ = near a contact, 3+ = junctions)
